defect: GetEqualityComparer<T> uses the collision-resistant comparer only for types other than string (&& typeof(T) != typeof(string)), so string keys fall back to the default equality comparer even when HashCollisionResistant is on.
why: String keys are the usual vector for hash-flooding denial of service on untrusted input; the collision-resistant string comparer exists and is skipped, so hash collision resistance does not apply to them.
